breakfast.name: Pão de Queijo (Cheese Bread)
breakfast.description: Puffy, cheese-filled bread rolls made with cassava flour and cheese. A beloved Brazilian breakfast staple.
ingredients: 2 cups shredded cheese (Gruyère or mozzarella preferred)
instructions: Preheat oven to 375°F
In saucepan, combine milk, oil, and salt
Bring to boil
Remove from heat and stir in cassava flour until combined
Cool mixture slightly
Add eggs one at a time, beating well after each addition
Fold in shredded cheese and black pepper
Spoon batter into greased muffin tins or use two spoons to drop onto baking sheet
Bake for 18-20 minutes until puffed and golden
Serve warm, straight from oven
breakfast.notes: The batter will be thick and sticky. Best served warm when they're still puffy.
breakfast.fun_fact: Pão de queijo originated in Minas Gerais state and is eaten throughout Brazil for breakfast or as a snack. They puff up dramatically in the oven.
alternatives: Add jalapeños for spicy version
Make ahead and reheat (they deflate but still taste good)
Use different cheeses for flavor variation

breakfast.name: Açaí Bowl
breakfast.description: A healthy breakfast bowl made from açai berry puree topped with granola, fruits, and honey. Popular in Brazil's coastal regions.
instructions: Blend frozen açai with splash of milk or juice until thick
Pour açai mixture into bowls
Arrange banana slices on top
Sprinkle with granola
Add fresh berries
Drizzle with honey
Top with coconut flakes and almonds
Eat with spoon and fork
Serve immediately
breakfast.notes: Work quickly - the bowl starts melting as soon as it's made.
breakfast.fun_fact: Açai is native to the Amazon and has been eaten by indigenous peoples for centuries. It became popular worldwide as a 'superfood' in the 2000s.
alternatives: Add chocolate chips for sweeter bowl
Use different berries in season
Add granola to the blended açai for texture

lunch.name: Feijoada (Black Bean Stew)
lunch.description: Brazil's national dish - a hearty stew of black beans and various pork cuts. Served with rice, farofa, and orange slices.
instructions: Soak black beans overnight or use quick-soak method
In large pot, heat oil and cook bacon until crispy
Remove bacon; brown pork shoulder and ribs
Add onions and garlic; cook until soft
Return bacon to pot with drained beans
Add bay leaves, cumin, coriander, and black pepper
Cover with water or broth
Bring to boil, then reduce heat and simmer covered for 1.5 hours
Add sausage and continue simmering another 30 minutes
Beans and meat should be very tender
Season with salt
Serve in bowls with rice, farofa, and orange slices on the side
The cooking liquid (caldo) is part of the dish
lunch.notes: Feijoada is traditionally made a day ahead to develop flavors. It's a thick, hearty stew.
lunch.fun_fact: Feijoada has roots in Afro-Brazilian cuisine and was historically made with leftover parts of pig, making it both economical and delicious. It's the ultimate comfort food in Brazil.
alternatives: Vegetarian version with mushrooms and beans
Quick version with canned beans
Lighter version with less pork

lunch.name: Moqueca (Fish Stew)
lunch.description: A rich, aromatic Brazilian fish stew with coconut milk, dendê oil, and fresh herbs. Typical of Bahia region.
ingredients: 1.5 lbs firm fish fillets (mahi-mahi or similar)
instructions: Heat dendê oil in large pot
Add sliced onions and cook until soft
Add garlic and cook 1 minute
Add tomatoes, bell pepper, and cumin
Cook for 5 minutes
Pour in coconut milk and bring to simmer
Carefully place fish fillets in stew
Simmer gently for 12-15 minutes until fish is cooked through
Add cilantro, coriander leaves, lime juice
Season with salt and pepper
Serve in bowls over white rice
lunch.notes: Dendê oil (palm oil) is essential for authentic flavor but can be hard to find. Use olive oil if necessary.
lunch.fun_fact: Moqueca is the signature dish of Bahia, the heart of Afro-Brazilian culture and cuisine. The combination of fish, coconut, and dendê oil reflects the African diaspora influences.
alternatives: Shrimp instead of fish for different protein
Olive oil instead of dendê oil
Add okra for authentic touch

dinner.name: Churrasco (Brazilian BBQ)
dinner.description: Brazilian-style grilled meats served in rodizio style (servers bring skewers to your table). A celebration of meat.
ingredients: Rice and black beans for sides
instructions: Prepare coals for hot charcoal grill or use gas grill on high
Mix salt, garlic, pepper, oregano, and cumin
Season all meats generously with spice mixture
Let meats sit for 15 minutes
Place beef ribs on grill first (they take longest)
Grill for 30-40 minutes, rotating occasionally
Add chicken and pork ribs
Grill for additional 20-25 minutes
Add steaks in final 5-10 minutes
Brush with chimichurri periodically
Meat should be charred outside, pink inside
Serve with grilled rice, black beans, farofa, and fresh salad
dinner.notes: The key is proper heat management and knowing when each meat is done.
dinner.fun_fact: Churrasco comes from the Gaucho tradition of the southern Brazilian states. It's served in rodizio restaurants where servers continuously bring grilled meats until you've had enough.
alternatives: All beef for steak lovers
All chicken for lighter version
Oven roasting instead of open fire

snacks.name: Pastel (Fried Pastry)
snacks.description: A crispy fried pastry filled with meat, cheese, or vegetables. Popular street food served at fairs and parties.
instructions: Make dough: Mix flour, salt, and sugar
Add butter and work with fingertips
Gradually add water and beer until dough forms
Rest dough 15 minutes
Make filling: Brown ground beef
Add onion and garlic; cook until soft
Mix in cheese; season with salt and pepper
Cool filling
Roll dough thin and cut into 3x4 inch rectangles
Place 1.5 tbsp filling on each rectangle
Fold in half and seal edges with fork
Heat oil to 350°F
Fry pastels until golden brown (2-3 minutes per side)
Drain on paper towels
Serve hot with hot sauce
snacks.notes: Beer in the dough makes it extra crispy. The filling should be cooled before assembly.
snacks.fun_fact: Pastel is one of Brazil's most beloved street foods. You'll find pastel stands everywhere from street fairs to football games.
alternatives: Spinach and cheese filling for vegetarian
Shrimp filling for seafood version
Baking instead of frying

desserts.name: Brigadeiro (Chocolate Truffle)
desserts.description: Small chocolate candy coated in sprinkles. Brazil's most iconic dessert, served at birthday parties and celebrations.
instructions: In saucepan, combine condensed milk, cocoa powder, and butter
Heat over medium heat, stirring constantly
Continue cooking and stirring for 8-10 minutes
The mixture should thicken and pull away from sides
Remove from heat and let cool slightly
Spoon onto parchment paper or oil surface
When cool enough to handle, roll into balls
Coat generously in chocolate sprinkles
Place in small paper cups
Refrigerate until serving
desserts.notes: The mixture burns easily, so constant stirring is essential. Cool slightly before rolling so it doesn't burn your hands.
desserts.fun_fact: Brigadeiro is said to be named after a Brazilian Air Force Brigadier (Brigadeiro in Portuguese) who was a favorite at parties. They're essential to every Brazilian birthday party.
alternatives: Add 1 tsp vanilla extract for flavor variation
Roll in finely chopped nuts instead of sprinkles
Dulce de leche version for different flavor

desserts.name: Pavlova (Meringue Cake)
desserts.description: A crispy meringue base topped with whipped cream and fresh fruit. Light and elegant Brazilian celebration dessert.
instructions: Preheat oven to 300°F
Beat egg whites until soft peaks form
Gradually add powdered sugar while beating
Continue beating until stiff, glossy peaks form
Fold in cornstarch, vinegar, and vanilla
Draw 8-inch circle on parchment paper
Spoon meringue onto parchment, forming nest shape
Bake for 1.5 hours at 300°F until pale golden
Turn off oven and cool completely inside
Whip heavy cream with sugar until stiff peaks form
Top meringue with whipped cream
Arrange fresh berries on top
Serve immediately or chill until serving
desserts.notes: Humidity affects meringue. Make on dry days for best results.
desserts.fun_fact: Though named after Russian ballerina Anna Pavlova, pavlova is extremely popular in Brazil as an elegant dessert for special occasions.
alternatives: Use different fruits in season
Chocolate drizzle on the meringue
Store-bought meringue bases to save time

drinks.name: Agua Fresca (Fresh Water)
drinks.description: A refreshing drink made with fresh fruit, water, and sugar. Perfect for hot Brazilian climate.
ingredients: 2 cups fresh fruit (watermelon, mango, or guava)
instructions: Cube fresh fruit
In blender, combine fruit, water, and sugar
Blend until smooth
Strain through fine mesh into pitcher
Add lime juice
Chill thoroughly
Serve over ice
Garnish with fresh mint and fruit slice
drinks.notes: Use whatever fruit is in season for best flavor.
drinks.fun_fact: Agua fresca is incredibly popular in Brazil and throughout Latin America during hot months. It's a cooling, refreshing drink with pure fruit flavor.
alternatives: Different fruits for variety
Sparkling water instead of still water
Herbs like basil or cilantro for flavor

drinks.name: Caipirinha (Lime Cocktail)
drinks.description: Brazil's national cocktail - a refreshing mix of cachaça, lime, sugar, and ice. Perfect for tropical heat.
instructions: Place lime wedges and sugar in glass
Gently muddle to release lime juice and dissolve sugar
Don't crush the lime - just press gently
Fill glass with ice
Add cachaça
Stir well
Garnish with lime wheel
Serve immediately
drinks.notes: Use fresh limes and don't over-muddle or the lime peel becomes bitter.
drinks.fun_fact: Caipirinha became Brazil's official national cocktail. Cachaça is a spirit made from sugarcane that's uniquely Brazilian.
alternatives: Vodka instead of cachaça for less authentic version
Add mint for fresh variation
Batch version for parties
